card.keepWhy: Church was people before it was a building.
sources: Acts 18:1-3 (Paul comes to Corinth and finds Aquila, a Jew born in Pontus, recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all Jews to leave Rome; being of the same trade, tentmakers, he stays and works with them)
Acts 18:18-19 (they sail with Paul to Ephesus)
Acts 18:24-26 (Apollos, an eloquent man of Alexandria, knowing only the baptism of John; Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more accurately)
1 Corinthians 16:19 (“Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in their house”)
Romans 16:3-5 (Prisca and Aquila risked their necks for Paul; “greet the assembly that is in their house”)
1 Corinthians 12:12-27 (one body, many members; “you are the body of Christ”)
Matthew 18:20 (“where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them”)
1 Corinthians 1:12 (“I follow Apollos”), linked to day 15; 1 Corinthians 3:5-9 (“I planted. Apollos watered”), behind the hard question

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when you hear the word “church,” what do you picture first?
options: most people do. this story might change the picture.
then you’re already close. let’s meet two of them.
i hear you. stay with me. this one is about a kitchen table.

steps.line: Priscilla and Aquila were a Jewish couple, tentmakers. When the emperor forced Jews out of Rome, they packed up and moved to Corinth.
steps.label: Acts 18:2

steps.line: Then Paul arrived, a tentmaker too. He lived with them, and the three of them sewed tents side by side.
steps.label: Acts 18:3

steps.q: Later, in Ephesus, they hear a gifted preacher, Apollos, who knows only part of Jesus’s story. What do you guess they do?
o: Take him aside and explain it more fully
Correct him in front of everyone
steps.why: Quietly, kindly, in private. And he became a great teacher.

steps.line: In Ephesus they heard a gifted preacher, Apollos. Instead of correcting him in public, they took him aside and explained the way of God more fully.
steps.label: Acts 18:26

steps.line: People gathered in their home to pray and share bread. Paul wrote, “Greet the church that is in their house.”
steps.label: Romans 16:3-5

steps.q: Paul calls a group of people in a living room “the church.” What does that tell you about the word?
o: They couldn’t afford a real church yet
Church first meant the people, not the place
They were hiding from the authorities
steps.why: There were no church buildings yet. The church was the people, wherever they met. Purpose-built churches came much later.

steps.q: Paul later wrote to the church in Corinth, which had split into camps, that it was like one body. Which parts did he say the body can least do without?
o: The head that leads the rest
The eyes that see the way
steps.why: 1 Corinthians 12: the parts that seem weaker are indispensable, and the less honoured get more honour. He wrote it to a church split into camps.

steps.line: Paul said they were like one body: eyes, hands, feet, every part needed. “You are the body of Christ.”
steps.label: 1 Corinthians 12:27

steps.q: In four of the six times the New Testament names this couple, she comes first: Priscilla and Aquila. Why do readers notice?
o: She was the one who sewed the tents
Listing the wife first was unusual then
steps.why: In that world husbands usually came first. Many readers take it as a sign Priscilla was the better known, maybe the lead teacher, of the two.

say: here’s what i love. the first churches had no steeples. they had kitchens, and people who opened their doors.
the new testament word for church, ekklesia, means an assembly, people called together. jesus said, “where two or three are gathered in my name, i am there among them.”

steps.q: Remember the church in Corinth that split into camps, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos”? Knowing this story, what’s surprising about that?
o: Paul’s own friends had taught Apollos
Apollos and Paul never once met
steps.why: Paul’s housemates helped teach Apollos. The camps fought over two men who were on the same team.

today.say: find two or three. message one or two people today and set up a meal, a walk, or a prayer together this week. that’s how the first churches started. if you already belong to a church, invite someone along.
options: good. send it today, while it’s fresh.
start small. one text, one coffee. two is enough.
